proof_obligations.statement: On origin/feat/42-bridge-production-clients at 5111108, engine/src/analysis/open_intelligence/bridge_native_clients.py BridgeWarehouse.read_job (lines 124 to 141) sends jobs.get for one job under the serving identity listening-post-staging, and production_bridge_clients (line 421) hands it to the admission as read_native_job. engine/src/analysis/open_intelligence/general_question_context_admission.py line 867 calls it for every creation record of the capture, and engine/src/analysis/open_intelligence/source_estate_bridge_result.py line 75 requires the job's user_email to equal the capture's child_service_identity, so the job is never the serving identity's own. Google's job page (https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-jobs) asks for bigquery.jobs.get to view the metadata of any job, and the retained roles/bigquery.jobUser carries bigquery.jobs.create only. The custom role CaptureJobRead holds bigquery.jobs.get and nothing else; the applier creates it with exactly that list, and its definition is read back and checked against the pin before the binding counts as proven. BigQuery has no resource below the project for a job, so the grant lets the serving identity read the metadata and query text of any job in the project; it carries no list, update, cancel or delete permission. The validator admits the role for this one member at project level with no condition.

The release and proof rows on sp_read_open_intelligence_execution_result_chain_v2 are correct only once the P3 caller slices move release_open_intelligence_run.py (L198, L517 to L518) and issue_r3_execution_proof.py (L136) from the v1 chain reader to sp_read_open_intelligence_execution_result_chain_v2. Step 6 must verify that by a readback of the caller code at the candidate commit before the first native run; until then a native run of release or proof would call the v1 reader and fail on permission.

The three amendment e rows on ogilvy-trends-v2-execution-approvals-staging open by allow lists of object name prefixes, and the replace row also uses resource.name.endsWith. Step 6 readback must prove native acceptance of each condition as written (the read row carries 11 logical operators, inside the 12 an IAM condition takes); that intelligence-42-orchestration can replace a slot control object and the collection day index under a generation match; that it cannot delete or replace any other object under 42/daily/, including one under 42/daily/authority/, 42/daily/certification/, 42/daily/grants/ or a prefix no row names; and which error a second create under ifGenerationMatch 0 returns on a create once prefix (a precondition failure, or a permission refusal because the overwrite would need objects.delete); either refuses, and the record stays.

The runner, not IAM, bounds roles/run.jobsExecutorWithOverrides on intelligence-42-daily-staging: before the first unattended run Step 6 must read the runner at the candidate commit and confirm it admits exactly one override, DAILY_DERIVATION_ID, and refuses runtime_override_forbidden for anything else (ops/runners/managed_runtime.py).

Secret Manager attaches IAM to the secret, not the version. The version pin on SOCIALCRAWL_OGILVY_API_KEY is expressed as a resource.name condition on the secret. Step 6 readback must prove native acceptance of that condition and that the job references the version by number so resource.name is evaluable.

In engine/src/analysis/open_intelligence/general_question_context_queries.py, _RESULT_SQL_V2 (line 940) reads open_intelligence_execution_consumptions_v2 (lines 941 and 944), open_intelligence_execution_approvals_v2 (line 947) and open_intelligence_execution_results_v2 (lines 949 and 951), and _APPROVAL_SQL_V2 (line 958) reads open_intelligence_execution_approvals_v2 (lines 959 to 960); the table names are pinned at lines 924 to 932. Each table is a read only manifest row and carries table level roles/bigquery.dataViewer for the serving identity alone, with no condition; the query jobs run under the retained roles/bigquery.jobUser. Step 6 reads each table's IAM policy back and confirms the serving identity can read no other table in the dataset.

The code this row serves is pending: the lane feat/42-bridge-run-record-binding, cut from feat/42-bridge-production-clients and not yet pushed when this row was written, binds the bridge run record, whose execution is named by the approval ledger's open_intelligence_execution_results_v2 row, by reading the funded pilot job's Cloud Run v2 execution (projects/ogilvy-trends-v2/locations/us-central1/jobs/intelligence-42-funded-pilot-staging/executions/<id>) with one GET as the serving identity. That GET needs run.executions.get. Google's Cloud Run role reference (https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/iam/roles) lists no predefined role narrower than roles/run.viewer that carries run.executions.get (admin, developer, editor and sourceDeveloper are broader), so the row binds roles/run.viewer on this one job for the serving identity; the funded account's existing viewer row on the job stays, and the validator admits the role there for no other member. On a job the role also reads the job, its executions and tasks and the job's IAM policy, and writes nothing. Before the row counts as proven, Step 6 reads the lane's code at its candidate commit and confirms it makes that single GET on an execution of this job and no other Cloud Run call; if the GET also needs run.jobs.get, roles/run.viewer already carries it. The ingest job intelligence-42-ingest-staging gets no serving identity row.

The v3 bridge clones read intelligence_42_sources_staging under roles/bigquery.dataViewer and write trends_v2_staging under the existing roles/bigquery.dataEditor. Google's table snapshot page (https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/table-snapshots-create) lists, on the source, bigquery.tables.get, bigquery.tables.getData, bigquery.tables.createSnapshot, bigquery.datasets.get and bigquery.jobs.create (dataViewer carries the first four, the project level roles/bigquery.jobUser the fifth), and on the destination dataset bigquery.tables.create and bigquery.tables.updateData, both in dataEditor. A snapshot with an expiration time also needs bigquery.tables.deleteSnapshot on the destination, which only dataOwner, admin and studioAdmin carry. Lead ruling, pending Albert's card: the v3 snapshots carry no expiration_timestamp, so the destination needs only bigquery.tables.create and bigquery.tables.updateData and no bigquery.tables.deleteSnapshot, and amendment e adds no binding for it. The plan change that drops the expiration from engine/src/analysis/open_intelligence/source_estate_bridge_plan.py lands separately on the bridge branch. The first native capture must confirm that nothing beyond these is asked. The custom role SourceSnapshotCreate is not bound by amendment e.

No scheduler binding is proposed and the deploy identity holds no actAs on the scheduler account; the operator who creates the two scheduler jobs is the principal that needs roles/iam.serviceAccountUser (actAs) on intelligence-42-scheduler, and that grant is made to the operator at provisioning time, as decision c of R03_DECISIONS_APPROVAL_20260913.json records.
